description: The plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for several variants of large language models, including a baseline “Vanilla” model and multiple configurations of the proposed SepLLM method, alongside StrmLLM for comparison. The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” spans from 0 to 140,000 with major tick marks at intervals of 20,000, using a linear scale. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 with major tick marks every 0.1 unit, also on a linear scale. Six distinct lines are plotted: “Vanilla” (purple, solid line) starts at approximately 3.35 and decreases steadily to around 2.55; “StrmLLM (n=64)” (blue, solid line) begins near 3.35 and drops to about 2.62; “SepLLM (n=64)” (orange, solid line) starts slightly below 3.35 and converges to approximately 2.58; “SepLLM (n=64, H)” (green, solid line) begins near 3.3 and ends around 2.57; “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (red, solid line) starts at ~3.3 and stabilizes near 2.56; and “SepLLM (n=128)” (dark blue, solid line) begins at ~3.35 and declines to ~2.60. All lines exhibit a rapid initial drop in loss followed by a slower, gradual convergence, with the “Vanilla” model consistently achieving the lowest loss throughout the training iterations.
